analysis.session_summary: The dollar was the weakest major despite a strong CB Consumer Confidence beat (103.3 vs 92.4), while the Swiss franc and New Zealand dollar led. EUR/USD rose 88.8 pips and GBP/USD 106.0 pips, with USD/CHF down 79.2 pips and USD/CAD down 103.7 pips. Tariff headlines from WSJ and Iran risk kept VIX bid, but most major leg moves had no single clear catalyst. The tape shows broad USD underperformance and risk-sensitive weakness in AUD and JPY.

themes.theme: Broad USD underperformance despite upbeat US consumer confidence
themes.evidence: CB Consumer Confidence beat forecast 103.3 vs 92.4 and had normal USD-positive reaction (+0.093%), yet DXY fell 71.3 points (-0.683%) and EUR/USD +88.8 pips, GBP/USD +106.0 pips.

themes.theme: Safe-haven CHF and high-beta NZD outperform while AUD and JPY lag
themes.evidence: CHF rank 1 (+0.364%), NZD rank 2 (+0.363%) versus AUD -0.221% and JPY -0.538%; USD/CHF fell 79.2 pips, CHF/JPY rose 171.2 pips.

themes.theme: Geopolitical tariff and Iran headlines underpinned risk repricing
themes.evidence: Top headlines included U.S. Prepares To Raise Tariffs On China And Other Countries at 14:00 and Trump administration officials debating targeting Iran's leaders at 17:00; VIX rose 1.353%, USD/MXN +2140.4 pips, USD/ZAR +955.9 pips.

currency_drivers.USD: US consumer confidence beat but failed to lift the dollar; risk-off positioning dominated.
currency_drivers.EUR: No own catalyst; strength was passive against a weak dollar.
currency_drivers.JPY: No own catalyst; initial bid failed and finished weakest despite risk headlines.
currency_drivers.GBP: No own catalyst; closed at best, supported as high-beta against weak dollar.
currency_drivers.AUD: No own catalyst; rally rejected, undermined by China tariff headlines.
currency_drivers.CAD: Macklem speech left CAD firmer 0.110%; no forecast to score surprise.
currency_drivers.CHF: No own catalyst; safe-haven demand kept it strongest against weak dollar.
currency_drivers.NZD: No own catalyst; closed at best, outperforming commodity peers.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: The single up leg of 85.1 pips had no clear catalyst; the nearest FOMC Williams item was too weak to own the move.

polarity_reads.read: The confidence beat produced a brief USD bid (+0.093%) but did not reverse the day's weak-dollar trend; positioning was short USD into the number.
CAD firmed 0.110% without a forecast to score, leaving the reaction as modest CAD-positive but not a clean surprise read.

scenarios.name: Soft USD persists into US data
scenarios.thesis: Dollar weakness continues as markets fade the consumer confidence beat and await benign US GDP/PCE.
triggers: Core PCE m/m prints at 0.3% or lower
Prelim GDP q/q at 3.5% or lower
scenarios.invalidation: Core PCE m/m above 0.3% or Prelim GDP q/q above 3.5%

pair_paths.rationale: Continuation of today's one-way up leg toward the session range high.
High-beta GBP extends its close at the top of a 108-pip range.

scenarios.name: USD rebound on strong US data
scenarios.thesis: Strong GDP/core PCE revives the dollar and unwinds the day's short-dollar trend.

pair_paths.rationale: Pullback can retrace the 88.8-pip rally within the 98.1-pip range.
USD strength and firmer yields can push USD/JPY back through its 82.6-pip range.

scenarios.name: Risk-off safe-haven extension
scenarios.thesis: Tariff and Iran headlines intensify, lifting VIX and weighing on risk FX and USD/CHF.
triggers: New tariff escalation from U.S. officials
scenarios.invalidation: VIX drops below 24.339 and no new tariff headline

pair_paths.rationale: Safe-haven CHF demand can extend the 89.7-pip range decline.
Risk-sensitive AUD can test the downside of its 37.2-pip range.

risks.why_it_matters: Would reinforce risk-off and pressure AUD, MXN, ZAR while supporting CHF.
risks.watch: U.S. Prepares To Raise Tariffs On China And Other Countries -- WSJ; Donald Trump Iran headlines

risks.risk: AUD CPI surprises to the upside
risks.why_it_matters: High-impact CPI at 01:30 can reprice RBA expectations and reverse AUD underperformance.
risks.watch: CPI m/m 0.4% forecast; Trimmed Mean CPI m/m 0.3% forecast

risks.why_it_matters: Would challenge the weak-USD narrative and unwind EUR/USD, GBP/USD longs.
risks.watch: Core PCE Price Index m/m forecast 0.3%; Prelim GDP q/q forecast 3.5%

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: AUD CPI at 01:30 then US Core PCE/Prelim GDP at 14:30 are the next major catalysts; soft US data would cement the dollar's slide, while hot reads could spark a rebound.
